chapter: Clarinet fingering and the Tio family
title: Why a player must keep practising
summary: He says music stays with you only if you play daily; after five years off his fingers, lips and breath control have suffered.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: He'd change it just that quick. You know, he was so used to doing it, that he was perfect. He was perfected. Yeah. You see, that's what I tell you about music. If you play music every day, it stays with you. But if you stop for two years, three years, a year, and this way, and pick it up again, and then go back again, and then stop for two, three more years, it's not the same. No. Of course, I, me, I'm stopped now about five years. I stopped playing. Out, for about five years. Sometimes I don't touch this thing. Months and months. I don't touch it. I don't touch it. Yes. It ain't the same when you pick it up again. No.

It ain't the same. Well, your fingers done got all stiff and out of whack. Your lips done got bad. Your wind done got bad. You forget, you forget the breathing space that you would take on certain measures and passages. You see, you can take breathing space on certain passages and measures and just continue on through. Well, if you don't catch the right breathing space, you'll never make that passage all in one slur.
